paragraphs: A hardened aircraft shelter is a concrete arch with blast doors, built to survive a strike with a jet inside. Abandoned, it becomes something else entirely: the doors hang open, vegetation reaches the apron, and the aircraft inside is a hulk rather than an asset. That decay is the subject.
The mesh runs 377,758 polygons and 392,546 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, covering the shelter structure, the doors and the aircraft within.

At $199 and built to CheckMate specification, it suits military history and documentary visualisation, post conflict and urban exploration imagery, film and television, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.

A heavy duty automatic gearbox is a stack of planetary gear sets, clutch packs and a torque converter, all inside a casing that hides every bit of it. The cutaway is the entire value of this asset: it turns an aluminium lump into an explanation of how the drive actually gets from engine to axle.
The mesh runs 425,544 polygons and 424,513 vertices in quads and tris with mixed UV layout, with the density in the gear teeth, the clutch plates and the cut faces of the casing.

A generic heavy duty version sits on this page at the same $199. Both suit automotive and commercial vehicle engineering presentation, technical marketing and cutaways, maintenance and training material, trade show displays and games. Built to StemCell specification, on sale since 2026.

A muscular system without the skeleton is a specific teaching asset: origins and insertions become visible, and the relationship between muscle groups is easier to follow than when bone is competing for attention. It is the layer most often shown first when explaining movement.

The mesh is remarkably light at 7,408 polygons and 7,412 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and ships with 4 texture maps at 4096x4096. That split is deliberate: the form is carried by silhouette, the detail by texture.

This page carries five other builds, including rigged versions at $249 and builds prepared for Cinema 4D and Maya. Aimed at anatomy and physiology education, fitness and sports science material, medical courseware, character reference and games. On sale since 2018.

Architectural and social visualisation libraries are thin on older people and thinner still on older people doing anything. This figure is an elderly woman in gardening clothes, standing rather than posed for a catalogue, which is exactly the kind of person a community or housing render usually needs and rarely finds.
The mesh is light at 16,186 polygons and 12,145 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, which suits a figure placed in a wider scene.

At $199 and built to StemCell specification, it suits architectural and community visualisation, social care and housing material, agricultural and allotment scenes, editorial imagery and games. On sale since 2023.

A patrol boat in border force service is built for endurance in open water rather than for combat: a fine hull, a large superstructure with accommodation for long patrols, a boat launching arrangement aft and a single gun forward. The livery matters as much as the hull in identifying the role.

The mesh runs 1,762,439 polygons and 908,107 vertices in quads and tris. The UVs overlap, which is sound economy on a hull built from repeated plating, and the geometry sits in the superstructure and mast.

At $199 and built to StemCell specification, it suits maritime security and border force visualisation, naval and coastguard presentation, news and documentary graphics, port scenes and games. On sale since 2023.

A dodgem is a fibreglass shell on a steel floor pan, with a rubber bumper ring around it and a pole reaching up to the ceiling grid for power. That pole is the detail that makes the ride work visually, because without it the car is just a small vehicle. Including a rider gives it scale and purpose.
The mesh is efficient at 80,487 polygons and 82,400 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and it arrives rigged so the car can be posed or driven.

At $199 and built to CheckMate specification, it suits amusement park and fairground visualisation, leisure industry presentation, event and family imagery, film and television, and games. On sale since 2021.

The defining feature of this dinosaur is that its front legs are longer than its back ones, which tilts the whole body upward toward the neck. Almost every other sauropod is the other way round, and getting that slope wrong turns the animal into a generic long neck.

The mesh is light at 22,092 polygons and 22,912 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, but it ships with 7 texture maps all at 8192x8192 - the whole detail budget going into skin rather than into geometry.

A standing pose sits on this page at the same $199. Both suit palaeontology and natural history material, museum and exhibition displays, documentary work, children's education, film and television, and games. Built to StemCell specification, on sale since 2021.

Corporate visualisation has historically drawn from a narrow set of figures, and a rigged business woman with African American features fills a genuine gap in most people libraries. Rigged, she can be posed for a meeting, a presentation or a lobby rather than standing in one attitude.

The mesh is efficient at 21,477 polygons and 19,998 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and ships with 22 texture maps - 9 at 4096x4096 and 13 at 2048x2048 carrying the skin, the suit and the hair.
At $199 it suits corporate and architectural visualisation, business and recruitment material, presentation and editorial imagery, animation and games. On sale since 2015.

A vehicle carrier is a box with a bow: the hull is filled with decks from waterline to weather deck so cars can be driven aboard, which gives the ship enormous flat sides and a very high freeboard. It is one of the least ship shaped ships afloat, and that is entirely deliberate.
The mesh is efficient at 173,531 polygons and 204,017 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the geometry in the stern ramp, the hull vents and the superstructure.

A rigged build sits on this page at the same $199. Both suit shipping and automotive logistics visualisation, port and terminal scenes, supply chain presentation, documentary work and games. Built to StemCell specification, on sale since 2022.

A bare chassis is the part of a car that engineers argue about and buyers never see: the structure, the suspension mounting points, the subframes and the crash structure at each end. Showing it alone is how a manufacturer explains stiffness, safety or packaging without the body in the way.

The mesh runs 279,740 polygons and 284,584 vertices in quads and tris with mixed UV layout, and ships with 8 texture maps at a mix of sizes up to 4096x4906, carrying the metal finishes and the weld seams.
At $199 it suits automotive engineering and technical marketing, safety and crash structure presentation, cutaway and ghosted renders, education material and games. On sale since 2015.

A canard delta puts small foreplanes ahead of the main wing, which makes the aircraft agile and gives it a silhouette quite unlike a conventional fighter. Shown armed, the pylons carry stores, which changes the profile again and turns a clean airframe into an operational one.
The mesh is efficient at 130,276 polygons and 136,949 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the geometry in the canards, the intake and the weapons pylons.

A rigged build sits on this page at $209. The static model at $199 covers defence and military aviation visualisation, news and documentary graphics, strategic analysis material, film and television, and games. On sale since 2021.

A spacewalk suit built by a different programme is not simply a recoloured version of the familiar one: the joint bearings, the backpack shape and the helmet visor arrangement all differ, because each agency solved the same problems independently. Those differences are the whole reason to model it separately.
The mesh is efficient at 50,653 polygons and 53,436 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and it arrives rigged so the suit can be posed on a figure.

Two more rigged builds share this page at the same $199, prepared for Maya and for Cinema 4D. Aimed at space industry visualisation, documentary and news graphics, museum and education material, film and television, and games. Built to CheckMate specification, on sale since 2024.

A commuter ferry is built for turnaround rather than for voyage: wide doors at both ends or amidships, benches instead of cabins, and a hull shallow enough for a river. Everything is arranged so that a full load can get off and another get on in under a minute.
The mesh runs 304,603 polygons and 327,539 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the geometry in the passenger deck, the wheelhouse and the boarding arrangements.

This page carries a Staten Island variant at $199 and a version with a pier at $219. All suit urban transport and waterfront visualisation, city planning and tourism material, film and television, and games. Built to StemCell specification, on sale since 2025.

A fast response cutter is a patrol boat sized for a crew that lives aboard for days rather than hours: a stern launching ramp for a small boat, a gun forward, a substantial mast array and enough superstructure for accommodation. That launching ramp is what distinguishes the class at a glance.

The mesh runs 432,424 polygons and 453,597 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and ships with 24 texture maps at a mix of sizes up to 8192x8192, carrying the hull markings and the salt weathering.

This page also carries a mast with radar at $39 and an Island class patrol boat at $199. Aimed at coast guard and maritime security visualisation, search and rescue material, news graphics, port scenes and games. On sale since 2019.
